next_step: Finalize SOW and schedule on-prem POC lab window (2-week cadence)
blockers: hardware procurement lead time (security-approved GPU nodes)
notes:
Topline: large, mission-critical contact center for regional emergency response and defense support. Must be fully air-gapped for classified workflows; some non-classified channels allowed to route to private dedicated cluster. Primary goals: reduce AHT with agent assist, automated ticket summaries for shift handoffs, reliable tool-calling to internal case systems (offline sync mode required), survive 10x concurrent spikes during incidents.

Key constraints: on-prem only for classified queues, no persistent connections to hosted control plane during air-gapped ops, model updates must be staged via signed artifact bundles, HSM-backed keys (customer-managed), strict PII redaction + retention policy (30-90 day windows by queue).

Stakeholders: CTO (ops), Head of Contact Centers, Security PM, Procurement lead, Field ops managers. 

Quote from security PM: 'We cannot accept any pull-based updates, all artifacts must be pushed through guarded channels and verified. Auditable transcript immutability is a must.'

POC ask: demonstrate private deployment in air-gapped lab with sample Genesys/Avaya integration, show deterministic tokenization, streaming assistant with local fallback when model variant unavailable, and a plan for autoscaling/bursting using pre-provisioned GPU pools behind an internal dispatcher.

Redwood fit: Private deployment with customer-managed control plane, model pinning for cert/reg review, Optimize recommendations to reduce token costs, canary rollout for on-prem bundles.

Risks noted: procurement timeline + hardware delivery, potential need for FIPS 140-2 validation on KMS/HSM, engineering clearance window for on-site install, legal review for data residency when routing non-classified traffic to dedicated hosted zone.
